findings.evidence: grep -n "p\. 9": LipschitzBoundedIntegrand.lean:43, RealIntegral/OnCurve.lean:505; conflicting anchor: PwC1ImmersionOn.lean:60 cites "arXiv:1808.00997, p. 3" for HW's §2 immersion condition, and every other HW citation in TauCeti/Analysis/Contour (25 hits) is section-level (§2 / §3) only.
findings.fix: Either correct the page to the one where HW's proof of Prop 2.3 actually appears (and keep the claim only if the paper really performs the one-sided split), or drop the page and the fidelity claim in both places, citing as elsewhere in the repo: "arXiv:1808.00997, Proposition 2.3" / "§2", and state the one-sided corner splitting as this development's own device.
findings.issue: The references claim HW's proof of Prop 2.3 "handles a crossing at a corner via exactly this one-sided splitting, p. 9"; the same claim is repeated at TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/Winding/RealIntegral/OnCurve.lean:505 ("matching Hungerbühler–Wasem's own proof of Prop 2.3, which handles that case via the same one-sided splitting (arXiv:1808.00997, p. 9)"). This attributes the file's key technique to the paper at a specific page; the repo's only other page anchor for this paper puts HW's immersion condition Λ̇|_{[aₖ,aₖ₊₁]} ≠ 0 at p. 3 (PwC1ImmersionOn.lean:60), and Prop 2.3 follows Def 2.1/Prop 2.2 in the same §2, so a proof of Prop 2.3 on p. 9 (i.e. inside §3, the residue theorem) does not fit. If HW do not in fact split one-sided at corners there, the PR credits the paper for its own novel step and misrepresents the formalization as paper-faithful.

summary: Central sources (HW Prop 2.3, the roadmap target, and the in-repo/AINTLIB-derived infrastructure) are credited by name throughout, and the moved RealIntegral file keeps its Authors line and AINTLIB provenance. The one problem is an unverified page-level claim attributing this PR's one-sided corner-splitting technique to HW's own proof of Prop 2.3, repeated in two files.
